Indeterminate Forms and l'Hospital's Rule

0/0 and ∞/∞ limits by differentiating top and bottom, plus how to rewrite 0·∞, ∞−∞, 1^∞, 0⁰ and ∞⁰ first.

0 / 11 problems mastered

When plugging in gives 00\frac0000​ or ∞∞\frac\infty\infty∞∞​, the limit could be anything. l'Hospital's Rule says: differentiate the top and the bottom separately, then try the limit again. The homework (#1–69 odd) is mostly the same skill: recognise the form, rewrite it if needed, apply the rule (sometimes twice).

l'Hospital's Rule

If lim⁡f(x)g(x)\lim\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}limg(x)f(x)​ is 00\frac0000​ or ±∞±∞\frac{\pm\infty}{\pm\infty}±∞±∞​, then

lim⁡f(x)g(x)=lim⁡f′(x)g′(x).\lim\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\lim\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}.limg(x)f(x)​=limg′(x)f′(x)​.

Top' over bottom'. NOT the quotient rule.

0 · ∞ (product)

Rewrite as a fraction: fg=f1/gfg=\dfrac{f}{1/g}fg=1/gf​ or g1/f\dfrac{g}{1/f}1/fg​. Put the ln⁡\lnln on top when there is one.

∞ − ∞ (difference)

Combine into a single fraction (common denominator), or factor something out.

1^∞, 0⁰, ∞⁰ (powers)

Let y=fgy=f^gy=fg. Take ln⁡y=gln⁡f\ln y=g\ln flny=glnf, find lim⁡ln⁡y=L\lim\ln y=Llimlny=L (a 0·∞ form), and the answer is eLe^{L}eL.

Not indeterminate

05=0\frac{0}{5}=050​=0, 50\frac{5}{0}05​ (→ ±∞), ∞+∞\infty+\infty∞+∞, 0∞=00^\infty=00∞=0 and ∞⋅∞\infty\cdot\infty∞⋅∞ are NOT indeterminate. Don't use l'Hospital on them.

Traps

Using the quotient rule

l'Hospital is f′g′\frac{f'}{g'}g′f′​, the top and bottom differentiated separately. It is not (fg)′\big(\frac fg\big)'(gf​)′.

Not checking the form

Check before every application, including the 2nd and 3rd. Problem #11 shows what goes wrong.

Stopping at \(\ln y\)

For powers, lim⁡ln⁡y=L\lim\ln y=Llimlny=L means the answer is eLe^LeL, not LLL.

Thinking \(1^\infty=1\)

It's indeterminate. (1+3x)x→e3(1+\frac3x)^x\to e^3(1+x3​)x→e3, not 1.
